subject: DPA & Subprocessor Summary — procurement-friendly edits and console blurb
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>

Cc: Acme Legal Team <legal@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick DPA/Qs for procurement — need short public blurb

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Procurement is asking for a short, plain-English paragraph we can include in the statement-of-work and our internal RFP summary that explains: (1) where Acme customer data may move geographically when using Redwood's Hosted API, (2) whether Redwood uses subprocessors and how we notify customers, and (3) what contractual and technical safeguards (SCCs, encryption, attestations) Redwood provides.

I attached our questionnaire (Acme_DPA_Questionnaire_v2.pdf) with a few specific prompts — we mostly need one or two sentences for the public-facing procurement summary and a bit more detail for the legal team. Can you share a console-ready snippet we can paste into our procurement packet by EOD tomorrow?

Appreciate it,
Samantha
Legal & Vendor Risk, Acme Corp

  2) An expanded technical bullet list for Acme Legal with subprocessor handling, transfer mechanisms, and how customers can view controls in the console.

From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-05T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick DPA/Qs for procurement — need short public blurb

Samantha / Mateo — drafting below candidate text for the procurement one-liner and the legal bulleted annex. Please comment.

Procurement-friendly paragraph (single sentence):
"Redwood Inference operates its Hosted API from multiple cloud regions; customer data may be processed in the US, EU, or other regions where Redwood or its subprocessors operate; we use contractual safeguards (EU Standard Contractual Clauses where applicable) and technical protections (TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest) to protect data in transit and storage."

Legal annex (short bullets):
- Subprocessors: Redwood maintains a public subprocessor list (link in console) and provides 30 days' notice before adding new subprocessors; customers may request details for procurement reviews.
- Transfers: We rely on SCCs for transfers from the EEA to the US and use standard contractual and organizational safeguards; specific regional routing options are available in Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Evidence: We can provide SOC 2Type II summary, network diagrams, and redacted machine-level logs on request via an evidence package.

If this looks good, Kimberly — can you convert the paragraph to a console microcopy (sales-friendly) and add an inline link to the subprocessor map? Also, Samantha, let us know whether Acme prefers a per-region breakdown in the packet or the paragraph + link approach.

- Laura
Senior Manager, Trust & Policy, Redwood Inference

To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, mateo.alvarez@redwood.com

Thanks Laura — this helps a lot. For procurement, the one-liner + link is ideal for the initial packet. The legal team will ask for the annex during their review; can you add a single line that calls out whether we use subprocessors in APAC specifically? If you can confirm whether any subprocessors in APAC process customer content (not telemetry), that would be great.

Samantha
Vendor Risk, Acme Corp

On a separate note, I may need a DocuSign DPA link once we get through legal — I can send a request and copy your team when ready.
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-06T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick DPA/Qs for procurement — need short public blurb

Samantha — quick update and proposed console microcopy below.

Console microcopy (90-140 chars):
"Redwood may process customer requests in the US, EU, or other supported regions; we publish our subprocessor list and use SCCs and industry-standard encryption to protect transfers."

APAC subprocessors: Redwood does engage subprocessors that operate in APAC for monitoring and regional routing. For customer content (API request/response bodies), our default Hosted API deployment does not route content to APAC subprocessors unless a customer has explicitly selected a regional residency option that routes processing to APAC. We will provide a per-region subprocessor appendix on request.

Links to the console subprocessor map and evidence package have been dropped into the draft Google doc here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cDPA-plainlang-draft

Action items:
- Samantha: confirm paragraph + link approach for the procurement packet.
- Mateo: if Acme confirms, we'll prepare a DocuSign powerform for the DPA and attach the annex for legal (link to DocuSign will be shared).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Legal Counsel (Privacy), Redwood Inference
